name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: The single best cross-department improvement is to standardize a shared "decision log" template across all teams. This ensures every major choice—from creative direction to technical constraints—is documented in one place with clear ownership, reasons, and trade-offs. The trade-off is slower initial setup for faster alignment later. Engineering owns the template; all departments contribute entries.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s “shared decision log” risks becoming a graveyard of stale checkboxes—teams will dump half-baked reasons just to clear the template, not to inform future decisions. Instead, enforce a *living* artifact: a single, searchable “decision ledger” where every entry must cite a concrete future action or deadline; anything older than 90 days auto-expires unless renewed by the original decider. That settles it: the lead publishes the ledger with the purge rule and the first 10 entries within two weeks.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt Scriv’s “living decision ledger” with mandatory future-action citations. Every major choice—creative, technical, or operational—must include the next concrete step it triggers, ensuring entries stay useful instead of decorative. The trade-off is stricter upfront effort: teams must articulate follow-up actions, not just log decisions. This single artifact becomes the single source of truth for why we did what we did and what happens next.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s “living ledger” solves the graveyard problem but risks turning every decision into a bureaucratic audit—teams will game the system by padding entries with trivial next steps just to comply. Instead, enforce a *lightweight* artifact: a shared Notion board where every major choice gets a one-line summary, a link to the full rationale, and a single owner who updates it only when the decision’s impact changes. That settles it: low overhead, high signal, no checkbox theater.

name: Scope
text: Adopt Scriv’s “living decision ledger” with mandatory future-action citations. Every major choice—creative, technical, or operational—must include the next concrete step it triggers, ensuring entries stay useful instead of decorative. The trade-off is stricter upfront effort: teams must articulate follow-up actions, not just log decisions. This beats a graveyard of stale entries or a bureaucratic audit by forcing real accountability.

name: Scriv
text: The "living decision ledger" still risks becoming a compliance chore—teams will pad entries with trivial next steps just to check the box. Instead, enforce a *minimal* artifact: a shared Slack channel where every major decision gets a single, timestamped message with a future-action citation. The lead is the person who owns the decision’s outcome, and the artifact exists when the message is posted.

name: Reel
